newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FOCUS - Brazil CVRD sale delayed slightly.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Brazil CVRD sale delayed slightly.

text.p: A slight delay in the privatization of Brazilian mining colossus Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) has as much to do with public opinion and diplomacy as it does with economics, officials said Thursday.

The sell-off, due to be Latin America's biggest, was put back to April from the first quarter of 1997 ostensibly to allow independent analysts to evaluate new gold and copper finds before the government sets CVRD's base price.
But those finds are more likely to affect future mining concession prices and debentures on potential mineral discoveries than CVRD's net worth, the officials said.

"We have already carried out a study of the deposits (in Carajas), but decided to carry out another because of the media frenzy and heated emotions," said a spokeswoman for Planning Minister Antonio Kandir. "We thought it better to play it safe."

She added, "In fact, the mineral discoveries are more likely to affect the value of concessions and the debentures offered as guarantees of how much the new owners will pay for larger-than-expected finds than they will the base price."

The latest hiccup in the sale of the world's largest iron ore exporter came after a deluge of reports about "historic" finds in Carajas in Para state, near the existing Igarape Bahia gold mine and the Salobo gold, copper and silver project.
Politicians opposed to the CVRD sell-off and newspapers also said Carajas could significantly alter the value of the company, an assertion some government officials conceded was possible.
CVRD has repeatedly said it is too early to tell how rich the deposits are.

The government hastened to reassure markets politics did not play a role in the decision to delay CVRD's privatization, expected to begin with a block sale of 40-45 percent of voting shares, followed by an internal offer to employees and then a public offering.
"It is better to have a good privatization than to have a rigid timetable," said presidential spokesman Sergio Amaral in a late night briefing Wednesday.
A spokeswoman for the National Development Bank (BNDES) said the sale was definitely on, but the minimum price remained in doubt.
"We need more time to evaluate the company," she said.
Economic analysts generally were not surprised by the postponement, saying what was important was that the government remained committed to the sale.
Brazil's National Privatization Council (CND), which had been due to meet January 29, will now probably discuss the CVRD privatization February 6. That date still must be confirmed.

The Planning Ministry expects independent consultants Mineral Research Development Inc to have completed its study of the possible worth of Carajas by then, allowing the privatization council to start discussing CVRD's likely minimum price.
